hypotheses.subject: monthly-spend-feature
hypotheses.summary: The feature flag `monthly-spend-feature` was switched from off to on, rolling out from 14:46 (145 off / 55 on) to 100% on by 14:47. p99 latency jumped from its ~200ms baseline to 1891ms in the very first fully-rolled-out minute and stayed in the 950-1900ms range, with no deploy, no config change, no traffic change (steady 1200 rpm) and flat memory. The new monthly-spend code path on the account page is slow.

supporting_evidence.claim: "p99_ms": 1891 (baseline p99 ~195-202 for the preceding 85 minutes), request_volume unchanged at 1200

hypotheses.summary: Alternative reading: the latency arrives from a downstream service that only the monthly-spend code path calls, so the flag exposed an already-slow dependency rather than slow local code. The logs name no upstream call or timeout, so this is unsupported by the retrieved evidence beyond the tail-latency shape (p50/p95 flat, p99 spiking) that dependency stalls often produce.

supporting_evidence.claim: "p50_ms": 28, "p95_ms": 197, "p99_ms": 1891 - only the tail degrades, which is typical of a blocking remote call on a minority of requests
Only errors logged are 'ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection' - no upstream timeout or 5xx from a named dependency
